claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a dual-nanoprecipitate microstructure.
In situ ETEM combined with EDS can reveal dynamic elemental redistribution in the alloy's nanoprecipitates during high-temperature oxidation.
Elemental redistribution in the nanoprecipitates influences the alloy's oxidation resistance and degradation behavior.
The proposed experiment exposes the alloy to a controlled high-temperature oxidizing environment during in situ ETEM/EDS observation.
ETEM temperatures and oxygen partial pressures can be selected to mimic environments encountered in gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components.
The nanoprecipitates act as reservoirs for alloying elements.
The nanoprecipitates may undergo compositional changes during oxidation.
Oxidizing conditions trigger elemental migration within the nanoprecipitates.
Oxidizing conditions trigger phase transformations within the nanoprecipitates.
Elemental migration and phase transformations alter local chemistry and thereby affect oxidation behavior.
In situ ETEM/EDS will capture real-time structural changes and elemental redistribution in the nanoprecipitates.
The observed nanoprecipitate changes will correlate with enhanced or degraded oxidation resistance.
Cast and wrought versions of similar alloys have lower oxidation resistance than the additively manufactured alloy.
Cast and wrought versions of similar alloys exhibit less pronounced nanoprecipitate evolution.
Electron-beam exposure may alter oxidation kinetics during ETEM observation.
Oxidation behavior observed in an ETEM specimen may not fully represent bulk-alloy behavior.
